title: Finite-cover Cech fibres have the same component labels after base change
statement: Let $p:Z\to S$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], let $h:U\to S$ be any scheme morphism, and let $b_U$ be a geometric point of $U$ with image $b$ in $S$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. Put $Z_U=U\times_SZ$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Projection induces a bijection $\pi_0((Z_U)_{b_U})\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_0(Z_b)$ between the sets of connected components of the two geometric fibres. In particular this applies to every finite iterated fibre product $Z^{(q)}=Z^{\times_S(q+1)}$, $q\ge0$.

source.place: Lemma 2.6.1, printed p. 5: the canonical component bijection; no additional Cech or arbitrary-map compatibility is asserted.

proof.text: Write $b=h\circ b_U:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ for the image geometric point. By [def-weil-geometric-point], the same algebraically closed field \Omega is used for both geometric fibres. Applying the universal property and uniqueness of [def-pc-fibre-product] twice gives a canonical isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\times_U(U\times_S Z)\cong\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\times_S Z$. It intertwines the projection-induced map to $Z$ and the maps to $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Hence the two geometric-fibre schemes are isomorphic, and the resulting homeomorphism carries connected components bijectively; this is the stated projection bijection.

source.place: Lemma 2.6.1, printed p. 5; canonical component bijection reconstructed from fibre-product associativity

proof.text: For $q\ge 0$, let $p_q:Z^{(q)}=Z^{\times_S(q+1)}\to S$ be the structure morphism. The case $q=0$ is the given finite map $p$. If $p_q$ is finite, the projection $Z^{(q+1)}=Z^{(q)}\times_S Z\to Z^{(q)}$ is the base change of $p$, hence finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence](a); its composite with $p_q$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition]. Induction gives that every $p_q$ is finite. Applying the first step to $p_q$ and $h$ gives the asserted component bijection for every finite iterated fibre product.
